Westphalian statesman Clemens August Heeremann von Zuydwyk, born at Surenburg in 1832, spent the Kulturkampf defending the Church in parliament and became chairman of the Centre Party in the Prussian Diet. A law student at Bonn, Heidelberg, and Berlin, he entered the Prussian Diet in 1870 and the Reichstag in 1871. He then resigned government office in 1875 to fight full-time for the oppressed Church.

His chief battle was against the law of May 1875 that threatened charitable orders nursing the sick. There he won important softening amendments, and he later led debates on the tariff, schools, and fine arts. An art critic who wrote on Westphalia's oldest panel painting and founded a magazine of Christian art, he served as Diet vice-president and honorary Centre chairman until his death in 1903.

Paul Looyen joins Danny Jones for an episode of the KONCRETE Podcast, numbered 78, to claim that humans are making black holes on Earth. Looyen brings a physics claim that sounds like science fiction. Jones hosts the talk.

Looyen lays out the tests and machines he says can birth tiny black holes. He weighs what such holes would do and how fast they would fade. Jones asks what the big labs say to the claim. Listeners with a love of wild physics get a bold hour. The library holds the talk as an archive record of the guest's stated claim.
